chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Abu Ali al-Kazzaz, from Dawud al-Raqqi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'O Dawud, having your hand inserted into the mouth of a dragon up to the elbow is better for you than seeking your needs from one who has not yet come to be (i.e., the wealthy/powerful who are not yet accessible or worthy).'

key_terms.التِّنِّين: Dragon, used metaphorically for a powerful or wealthy person
key_terms.الْمِرْفَقِ: Elbow, indicating the depth of insertion
key_terms.لَمْ يَكُنْ فَكَانَ: Has not yet been but then became, referring to the rise of the wealthy/powerful

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by 'hand in the mouth of the dragon' regarding seeking needs from others?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses the vivid metaphor of inserting one's hand into a dragon's mouth to illustrate the severe discomfort of seeking sustenance from those who are not truly self-sufficient or are prone to pride. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on *istighna* (dignified independence) and warns against the spiritual degradation of *tabarruj* (displaying need) before the powerful, prioritizing inner dignity over material ease.
